report.summary: Both failures share one root cause: the server accepts a year one past the current year. `validate_book` uses `this_year + 1` as the upper bound (app/main.py:83), but its own error message says 'between 1 and {this_year}', and both tests expect next year to be rejected. Fix the bound in app/main.py:83 to `this_year`; no test changes are needed.

causes.title: Book year validation accepts next year (off-by-one upper bound)
causes.explanation: validate_book allows years up to date.today().year + 1, so a book with year = current year + 1 is saved with HTTP 201 instead of being rejected with 422. The rejection message reads 'Year must be between 1 and {this_year}', which contradicts the code's bound. The API test sends year THIS_YEAR+1 and expects 422, and the UI test enters next year and expects the error to appear, so both tests encode the intended rule. The behaviour is deterministic for a given calendar year, so this is not flakiness. The year-zero case still passes because 0 is below the lower bound. The UI test would also fail its final assertion (no row for the title), since the book was actually created.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:66: AssertionError: assert 201 == 422 (response.status_code was 201 Created for year=THIS_YEAR+1)
app/main.py:84: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:42-44: books.add(title, "Someone", str(date.today().year + 1)); expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between")
UI aria snapshot: row "Future-5856a016 Someone 2027 Delete" was created, and get_by_test_id("error") found no element
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py:83 change `this_year + 1` to `this_year`, so the check reads `if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year:`. Keep the message as is. Re-run the API and UI tests for the next-year case.
